newsitem.title: UK: Granada chairman's repair plan hits shares.
newsitem.headline: Granada chairman's repair plan hits shares.

text.p: Gerry Robinson, chairman of British media and leisure group Granada Plc, sold 57,500 of his shares in the firm and caused a stock market stir on Monday but the group explained the cash was to repair one of his homes.
A deal that raised more than 500,000 pounds ($817,000) gross was worth nearer 300,000 net, a company spokesman said.
During the day Granada's stock price slid some 18 pence to about 895 pence, in trade of nearly five million shares, after the announcement that Robinson had sold at 914 pence on Friday.
The wider London stock market was flat on the day, but dealers told Reuters that news of Robinson's sale coincided with a bout of profit-taking in Granada.

"It is a sale to raise cash for a particular purpose, namely the restoration of his house in Ireland," a company spokesman told Reuters during the afternoon, adding that all Robinson's other interests in Granada shares and options remained intact.
Robinson retains an interest of 300,872 shares in Granada, according to the routine official notification of the sale which was published by the stock exchange.
Robinson's home in Ireland needs a new roof, the spokesman added. ($1=.6120 Pound)
